holidays.name: National Get Up Day
holidays.description: A day dedicated to the idea that when life knocks you down, you get back up. Celebrants are encouraged to shake off setbacks, dust themselves off, and take on the world again.
holidays.origin: Created by the Boston-based motivational group National Get Up Day Foundation, an informal observance that spread through social media and calendars of unofficial holidays.
holidays.funFact: The day is a good excuse to ditch the snooze button, since the average person hits snooze about three times before actually getting out of bed.

holidays.name: National Baked Alaska Day
holidays.description: A salute to the gloriously theatrical dessert made of cake and ice cream wrapped in meringue and briefly baked until golden brown. It's a dessert that is both hot and cold at once.
holidays.origin: The dessert is often linked to Delmonico's restaurant in New York, which created a version called the Alaska, Florida in 1867 to celebrate the U.S. purchase of Alaska. Its fiery reputation grew from there.
holidays.funFact: The meringue acts as an insulator, which is why the ice cream inside doesn't melt in the hot oven. Physicist Count Rumford studied this principle in the 1800s.

holidays.name: Serpent Day (Dragon Boat and Snake Appreciation Day variant) - Hot Chocolate Bomb-style Cocoa Cheer: National Texas Day Eve? No, Just Plain Spunky: Freedom Day
holidays.description: Freedom Day in the United States commemorates the day in 1865 when President Abraham Lincoln signed the joint resolution that became the 13th Amendment, abolishing slavery. It is observed with reflection, education, and celebration of liberty.
holidays.origin: Lincoln signed the resolution passing the 13th Amendment on February 1, 1865. Activist Major Richard Robert Wright Sr. championed the date, and Freedom Day became a national observance proclaimed in the 1940s.
holidays.funFact: Lincoln's signature wasn't actually required on constitutional amendments, which makes his signing a largely symbolic gesture that he made anyway.

holidays.name: Change Your Password Day
holidays.description: A nerdy observance urging everyone to retire their old, creaky passwords such as 'password123' and create stronger ones. Think of it as a spa day for your online accounts.
holidays.origin: Started in 2012 by Intel Security (formerly McAfee) as a lighthearted push for better digital hygiene. It lands on February 1 as a New Year's follow-up to cyber resolutions.
holidays.funFact: Year after year, '123456' and 'password' rank among the most commonly used passwords in the world.

holidays.name: Working Naked Day
holidays.description: An unofficial and cheeky day when remote workers are said to celebrate the freedom of working from home with a certain lack of dress code. Video calls are strongly discouraged.
holidays.origin: It originated in the late 2000s as an internet joke tied to the rise of telecommuting, gaining traction on blogs and unofficial holiday lists.
holidays.funFact: The rise of remote work has made this a running joke, with countless workers confessing to wearing business tops and pajama bottoms on video calls.
